newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold prices follow tumbling world prices.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold prices follow tumbling world prices.

text.p: Istanbul gold prices followed worldwide 12-year record lows on Monday while volume rose to 1,925 kilos from Friday's 1,250 kilos on some short covering as well as arbitrage deals, dealers said.
Gold closed sharply lower at $316.20 an ounce and 1,526,500 lira per gram, from $325.00 and 1,568,000 lira on Friday following a plunge in London after the U.S. opening.

"There is volatility and a negative mood after tumbling world gold prices. Nobody knows where the price will go to. But volume is lively in the domestic market, depending on arbitrage and position-taking deals. Seasonal factors also buoy the demand," said a private bank's gold trader.
He also said gold demand would rise if the free fall ended in the short term.
The Turkish currency firmed to 150,000 against the dollar from 150,200 at Friday's close, in line with the dollar's weaknes in the world markets.
Dealers said a firmer local currency also pulled down the lira term prices on the gold exchange.
Most of the day's trade -- 1,570 kilos -- took place in the morning session with 50.5 percent of the total volume conducted in lira terms.
